(a) Authority.—
        (1) In general.—The Director of the Missile Defense Agency is the technical authority of the Department of Defense for integrated air and missile defense activities and programs, 
including joint engineering and integration efforts for such activities and programs, including with respect to defining and controlling the interfaces of such activities and programs and the allocation of technical requirements for such activities and programs. 
        (2) Detailees.—
            (A) In carrying out the technical authority under paragraph (1), the Director may seek to have staff detailed to the Missile Defense Agency from the Joint Functional Component Command for Integrated Missile Defense and the Joint Integrated Air and Missile Defense Organization in a number the Director determines necessary in accordance with subparagraph (B). 
            (B) In detailing staff under subparagraph (A) to carry out the technical authority under paragraph (1), the total number of staff, including detailees, of the Missile Defense Agency who carry out such authority may not exceed the number that is twice the number of such staff carrying out such authority as of January 1, 2016.   
    (b) Assessments and Plans.—
        (1) Biennial submission.—Not later than January 31, 2017, and biennially thereafter through 2021, the Director shall submit to the congressional defense committees an assessment of the state of integration and interoperability of the integrated air and missile defense capabilities of the Department of Defense. 
        (2) Elements.—Each assessment under paragraph (1) shall include the following:
            (A) Identification of any gaps in the integration and interoperability of the integrated air and missile defense capabilities of the Department. 
            (B) A description of the options to improve such capabilities and remediate such gaps. 
            (C) A plan to carry out such improvements and remediations, including milestones and costs for such plan.  
        (3) Form.—Each assessment under paragraph (1) shall be submitted in classified form unless the Director determines that submitting such assessment in unclassified form is useful and expedient.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the biennial assessments and the detailing of staff as consultation or coordination. Both stay inside the federal government: the assessments go to congressional committees, and the detailees come from other Department of Defense organizations. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is brought into any federal decision, and the section requires no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Director shall submit to the congressional defense committees an assessment of the state of integration and interoperability of the integrated air and missile defense capabilities of the Department of Defense.

opus.w: The section gives the Missile Defense Agency technical authority, lets the Director bring in staff detailed from other DoD commands, and requires assessments to be sent to the congressional defense committees. Every one of these actors is inside the federal government. Sending reports to Congress and coordinating within DoD are not participation, and the section involves no outside party, comment period, hearing, or right to sue.
opus.s: the Director shall submit to the congressional defense committees an assessment of the state of integration and interoperability of the integrated air and missile defense capabilities of the Department of Defense.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this section involves participation. It has detailees, "joint" integration work, and assessments submitted to committees, all of which sound procedural. That reading fails because every actor named is federal: the Missile Defense Agency, DoD joint commands, staff detailed from those commands, and the congressional defense committees. No one outside the federal government is consulted on any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes internal coordination within the Department of Defense. The Missile Defense Agency, the Joint Functional Component Command, and the Joint Integrated Air and Missile Defense Organization are all federal entities. The detailing of staff and the submission of reports to congressional committees constitute intra-governmental activity, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: The Director may seek to have staff detailed to the Missile Defense Agency from the Joint Functional Component Command for Integrated Missile Defense and the Joint Integrated Air and Missile Defense Organization
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Joint Functional Component Command" or "Joint Integrated Air and Missile Defense Organization" are outside entities, or that the detailing of staff constitutes a form of consultation. However, these are all components of the Department of Defense (the federal government). The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or officials is not participation. Furthermore, the reports are submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government.
